scope: Fresh independent model audit of all 300 current targets, all 144 historical assistant turns, every distinct assistant word form, every lexical evidence entry, and every external word-choice rationale. Original data unchanged. Held-out/test/archive material not opened.
method: Read all user/assistant contexts and targets. Reviewed every distinct non-Dolch form and unique evidence wording linguistically; cross-checked every exact-Dolch claim against frozen JSON. Read the first100 prose rationales; verified all remaining200 templated rationales express their reviewed evidence with correct scope, with punctuation-only normalization when comparing text. Structural coverage checks supplement, not replace, phonics judgment. Brief secondary relevance/history/factual/safety/length checks flag clear material defects. Row hashes include exact original JSONL line bytes and newline.

findings.detail: requires_history=true, but final child turn “what about rain” explicitly supplies the rain topic and target “It can get you wet.” can be generated without any earlier turn. Revise the final short child turn to refer back to the selected topic without naming it, while preserving the required-history count and short bucket.

requires_history=true, but final child turn “the cold one” independently supplies the property paraphrased by “Not hot, then.” Earlier milk-choice history is unnecessary to the target. Revise the final short child turn so the earlier warm/cold alternatives are necessary.

requires_history=true, but final child turn “and what about cheese” names cheese and supports target “You can eat it.” without any earlier toy-bricks/cheese exchange. Revise the final short child turn to refer to the changed topic without restating cheese.

Target asserts “You put it there.” History only states marble locations and never says the child placed the green marble under the mat. This invents a factual event. Remove the unsupported sentence or replace it with a fact actually given in the context.
